messages.text: MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year joins Hundred final coverage

metadata.summary: The MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year for 2026, Rosa Simkin, received the ultimate competition prize when joining Sky Sports' live coverage of The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday.
metadata.content: Rosa Simkin: 2026 MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year winner joins Sky Sports for The Hundred final at Lord's | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Rosa Simkin: 2026 MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year winner joins Sky Sports for The Hundred final at Lord's MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year winner for 2026 is Rosa Simkin; the 18-year-old from Warwickshire, who is currently studying yournalism at Cardiff University, joined Sky Sports' live coverage of The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday as part of her prize Monday 17 August 2026 14:28, UK Image: Rosa Simkin interviews Trent Rockets' Georgia Adams for Sky Sports during The Hundred women's final at Lord's (image: Jed Leicester, MCC ) The MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year for 2026, Rosa Simkin, received the ultimate competition prize when joining Sky Sports' live coverage of The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday. During the innings break of both the women's and men's finals, Rosa held flash interviews talking to Georgia Adams from Trent Rockets and Noor Ahmad from Manchester Super Giants as both teams ultimately went on to lift the titles. The 18-year-old also presented some of the bitesize highlight videos for Sky Sports Cricket's digital channels and made content for Lord's Instagram, giving audiences an insight into her day as part of the team. metadata.summary: Nasser Hussain hailed new England Test captain Joe Root's decision to abolish a team curfew but fears the returning skipper sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader like his predecessor Ben Stokes.
metadata.content: Joe Root: England Test captain right to remove curfew, says Nasser Hussain ahead of three-Test Pakistan series | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Joe Root: England Test captain right to remove curfew, says Nasser Hussain ahead of three-Test Pakistan series Nasser Hussain: "I'm pleased Joe is doing it [Test captaincy], although I may have gone in the direction of Harry Brook"; watch the first Test of the three-match series between England and Pakistan, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10am, Wednesday (first ball 11am) Nasser Hussain Cricket expert and columnist Monday 17 August 2026 14:29, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Test captain Joe Root explains why he has removed the curfew that was previously imposed on his team Nasser Hussain hailed new England Test captain Joe Root's decision to abolish a team curfew but fears the returning skipper sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader like his predecessor Ben Stokes. Root has captained England on a record 65 occasions, most recently during their second Test defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended for breaking a team curfew that was introduced off the back of the 4-1 Ashes defeat in the winter. messages.text: Maresca's Man City problems are more than a missing midfield

metadata.summary: Enzo Maresca spoke of his desire to "close the gap" between Manchester City and Arsenal before watching his side suffer a painful 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield on Sunday. Perhaps the gaping holes through the spine of his team should be more of an immediate area of focus.
metadata.content: Man City's Community Shield defeat to Arsenal revealed the scale of the job facing Enzo Maresca on eve of new Premier League season | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Analysis Man City's Community Shield defeat to Arsenal revealed the scale of the job facing Enzo Maresca on eve of new Premier League season Enzo Maresca's Man City were exposed in brutal defeat to Arsenal in Community Shield; spine of side faced issues, particularly in midfield; Man City play first Premier League game against Bournemouth on Sunday, live on Sky Sports Main Event; kick-off 2pm Laura Hunter Football Features Writer Monday 17 August 2026 14:18, UK Image: Manchester City were thrashed 3-0 by Arsenal in the Community Shield Enzo Maresca spoke of his desire to "close the gap" between Manchester City and Arsenal before watching his side suffer a painful 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield on Sunday. Perhaps the gaping holes through the spine of his team should be more of an immediate area of focus. The manner of that loss has raised qualifying questions, the only real clarity offered by the Premier League champions. Mikel Arteta's side brutally exposed a series of City shortcomings: defensively disorganised, missing a midfield and lacking leadership, to name but a few. Under a week from the start of their campaign proper, City appear worryingly incomplete. metadata.content: The Hundred: Nasser Hussain praises quality of 2026 tournament but criticises packed schedule ahead of Pakistan Test series | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content The Hundred: Nasser Hussain praises quality of 2026 tournament but criticises packed schedule ahead of Pakistan Test series Nasser Hussain praised the quality of the 2026 Hundred, with 19 of the 22 players in the final being internationals, but criticised the packed schedule for England’s Test players ahead of Wednesday’s series opener against Pakistan, live from 11am on Sky Sports Nasser Hussain Cricket expert and columnist Monday 17 August 2026 13:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain says the one thing that stood out was the quality of the players from each team in The Hundred this season. Nasser Hussain has praised the quality of both domestic and international players in the Hundred, highlighting its strength compared with the Vitality Blast. The Manchester Super Giants edged out the Trent Rockets in a thrilling men's final at Lord's, with 19 of the 22 players involved having full international caps. New Zealand's Tim Seifert stole the show, smashing an imperious 72 off 38 balls. The three uncapped domestic players - Aneurin Donald, Ben Sanderson and Paul Walter - also impressed throughout the tournament, with Walter hitting 80 off 46 in the eliminator and Donald contributing a rapid 38 off 19 for the Rockets in the final.
